sentences.text: The Baggage Control System loads the approved sort plan and applies its effective time window before bags enter sortation.
Lantern is the operational alias used for the Flight Data Gateway in sortation coordination.
The Baggage Control System checks the plan against current flight and handling records before assigning a route.
The Concourse Zone Controller coordinates local conveyor availability with the active sort plan.
The Induction Tray Conveyor presents bags at controlled spacing so each bag can be identified before route selection.
The Primary Crossbelt Sorter applies the assigned destination and screening status to each identified bag.
The Primary Crossbelt Sorter sends a Chute Occupancy Note when a destination lane approaches its configured limit.
Route selection favors the approved path with adequate capacity and sufficient time for the planned handling.
The North Gate Scanner and South Gate Scanner verify bag identity at their respective route decision points.
A scan mismatch prevents the bag from continuing on a route that depends on the unresolved identity.
Congestion awareness uses current lane availability, conveyor stops, and the observed rate of incoming bags.
The Baggage Operations Supervisor sets local congestion thresholds and confirms the authorized response to sustained overload.
Tern is the operational alias used for the Baggage Operations Supervisor in sortation coordination.
When a planned lane is unavailable, the Baggage Control System selects an approved alternate route only if screening status and flight timing remain valid.
Bags with an unresolved destination or a route outside their handling limits are diverted to the Secondary Inspection Chute.
The Image Resolution Desk resolves image-related holds before affected bags are returned to normal sortation.
The Explosives Response Team manages security holds under the applicable response procedures.
A bag returns to normal handling only after its identity, examination outcome, and routing authorization agree.
The East Make-Up Conveyor and West Make-Up Conveyor are selected according to the active plan and available capacity.
The Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit operates within its assigned flight window and reports when its usable capacity is constrained.
The Transfer Bag Feeder continues to hold transfer bags until screening status and intended onward handling are confirmed.
The Bag Reconciliation Station compares bag identity with the active handling record and flags unresolved discrepancies.
The Bag Reconciliation Station sends a Bag Match Query when bag identity cannot be reconciled with the active handling record.
Bags found on a stopped or misdirected path are held from onward movement until their location and identity are established.
The Maintenance Technician isolates a failed conveyor section and confirms that the route is safe before service resumes.
The Baggage Operations Supervisor authorizes recovery to the approved sort plan after the cause of the abnormal path has been addressed.
